sheet-1-1.description: The northern half of the Midvale business street, drawn on the right side of Sheet 1 at 50 feet to an inch. The Midvale & Greenwood Lake Turnpike, today's Ringwood Avenue, runs up the middle of the part; it is crossed by 1st Avenue at the top, by Furnace Lane, and by Belmont Avenue at the bottom, while Stephens Avenue leaves it to the west and Laura runs parallel to it on the east between Furnace Lane and Belmont Avenue. A heavy line along the Erie Railroad's Greenwood Lake Branch bounds the part on the west; the area west of that line is the southern stretch of the same street, drawn as the second part of the sheet. Most buildings are frame dwellings with outbuildings. The commercial core lies at Furnace Lane: the Union House and the American House with saloons, a row of feed, store and auto buildings, a meat shop, and a brick general store and post office on the west side of the Turnpike, with a vacant store, a hardware store, a shed and a barber shop on the east side. Farther south stand the Midvale School, a brick building heated by steam, the Mechanics Hall, a pool and barber room and a garage. A Methodist Episcopal church heated by steam and a horse shed stand at the north end on the east side, and a water tower with a shed stands west of the Turnpike. The upper right corner carries the title cartouche, the fire and water facilities notes and a location map of New Jersey, which are masked out; the legend key at the top is masked out as well.
notes: Midvale & Greenwood Lake Turnpike is today's Ringwood Avenue.

The street printed Belmont Av. on this part is at the position of today's Melrose Avenue (checked against the spacing of the cross streets); today's Belmont Avenue is the street printed Melrose Av. on part 2.
Furnace Lane is today's Furnace Avenue; 1st Av. is today's 1st Street; Laura is Laura Avenue.
Water facilities: none; fire department of 60 volunteers with a chemical engine and a hook and ladder truck (sheet notes).

Midvale. Scale 50 ft to an inch. Two parts side by side, divided by a heavy line along the Greenwood Lake Branch: part 1 (right) the north stretch of the Midvale & Greenwood Lake Turnpike (Ringwood Avenue) from Belmont Av to 1st Av, with Stephens Av, Furnace Lane and Laura; part 2 (left) the south stretch from Depot Av to north of Melrose Av, with Erie Av and Laura. Sheet 'Melrose Av' is modern Belmont Avenue and sheet 'Belmont Av' is modern Melrose Avenue (positions checked against spacing). Key, title cartouche and location map masked out.

sheet-1-2.description: The southern stretch of the Midvale business street, drawn on the left side of Sheet 1 at 50 feet to an inch and separated from the northern stretch by a heavy line that follows the Erie Railroad's Greenwood Lake Branch. The Midvale & Greenwood Lake Turnpike, today's Ringwood Avenue, runs along the left edge with only its east side drawn; the margin beyond it is marked no exposure. Laura runs north from Melrose Avenue at the top, and Melrose Avenue, Erie Avenue and Depot Avenue cross from the Turnpike to the railroad. The blocks north of Melrose Avenue hold frame dwellings, a grocery and a blacksmith shop. The large block between Melrose and Erie Avenues contains the Midvale Hotel, a garage, an ice cream and soda shop, an ice house, and a row of dwellings on lots running back from Erie Avenue. South of Erie Avenue stand a fire department house with a jail, a dry goods store, a drug store, dwellings, an auto shed and the brick Columbia Hotel. At the foot of Depot Avenue are the Midvale-Wanaque railroad station and its passenger station beside the Greenwood Lake Branch tracks. A blank strip west of the Turnpike and the bottom margin, which points to Sheet 2, complete the part. The part of the legend key that reaches across the dividing line is masked out.
notes: Midvale & Greenwood Lake Turnpike is today's Ringwood Avenue.
The street printed Melrose Av. on this part is at the position of today's Belmont Avenue (checked against the spacing of the cross streets).
Depot Av. is today's Railroad Avenue.
Midvale-Wanaque R.R. Station on the Erie Railroad's Greenwood Lake Branch, since abandoned.

Midvale. Scale 50 ft to an inch. Two parts side by side, divided by a heavy line along the Greenwood Lake Branch: part 1 (right) the north stretch of the Midvale & Greenwood Lake Turnpike (Ringwood Avenue) from Belmont Av to 1st Av, with Stephens Av, Furnace Lane and Laura; part 2 (left) the south stretch from Depot Av to north of Melrose Av, with Erie Av and Laura. Sheet 'Melrose Av' is modern Belmont Avenue and sheet 'Belmont Av' is modern Melrose Avenue (positions checked against spacing). Key, title cartouche and location map masked out.

sheet-2-1.description: The southern end of Midvale toward Wanaque, the main part of Sheet 2, drawn at 50 feet to an inch with the street grid turned about fifteen degrees from the sheet's other part. The Midvale & Greenwood Lake Turnpike, today's Ringwood Avenue, runs down the right side of the part; Antigo crosses at the top, Lines Avenue leaves it westward, and Wausau Place and Mill Street run north and south off them. The Erie Railroad's Greenwood Lake Division runs along the right edge, with a switch curving southwest across the Turnpike to the Wanaque Paper Mill. Along the Turnpike north of Lines Avenue stand bake houses with ovens, groceries, a dry goods store and dwellings; St. Francis' Roman Catholic Church and a sisters' house, both of concrete block, face Lines Avenue. East of the Turnpike is the J. Gaston Drew flour, feed and hay business with a feed warehouse, flour warehouse and hay warehouse, and a row of dwellings on the east side south of Lines Avenue. The Reformed Dutch Church, stucco on frame, stands south of Lines Avenue. The lower half of the part shows property of the Wanaque Paper Company: warehouses, open coal bins, a platform, and the switch track, and the Wanaque post office, a builders' supply shed and the E. J. Ricker coal and lumber yard with coal pockets and lumber sheds along the railroad. The top left carries the north arrow; the title cartouche at the top right is masked out.
notes: Midvale & Greenwood Lake Turnpike is today's Ringwood Avenue.
Antigo appears to be today's Morningside Place, and Wausau Pl. the short northward stretch at its west end (Morningside Place in OpenStreetMap).
Mill St. is not in OpenStreetMap.
Several streets are marked Arbitrary (arbitrary street numbers).

Midvale / Wanaque. Scale 50 ft to an inch. Two parts divided by a heavy line: part 1 (main) the Turnpike from Antigo south past Lines Av, with Wausau Pl, Mill St, St Francis R.C. Church, Reformed Dutch Church, Wanaque Paper Co. and the Erie R.R. Greenwood Lake Div'n; part 2 (lower left) the Turnpike from Depot Av south to Antigo. Antigo is probably modern Morningside Place. Wausau Pl and Mill St are not in OpenStreetMap.

sheet-2-2.description: A short stretch of the Midvale & Greenwood Lake Turnpike, today's Ringwood Avenue, drawn at the lower left of Sheet 2 at 50 feet to an inch and separated from the sheet's main part by a heavy line running diagonally down the sheet. It continues Sheet 1 southward: Depot Avenue is at the top, with a general store and a garage on its south side, and Antigo crosses at the bottom. The Turnpike runs down the part with both sides drawn. The blocks on both sides are thinly built, with scattered frame dwellings, sheds and outbuildings, an auto repair shop and a wholesale liquor store near Antigo. A strip of the Erie Railroad's Greenwood Lake Division crosses the lower right corner of the part. The scale of feet at the bottom is masked out.
notes: Midvale & Greenwood Lake Turnpike is today's Ringwood Avenue; Depot Av. is today's Railroad Avenue.
Antigo appears to be today's Morningside Place.
